findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or repository access can retrieve and reuse these credentials to impersonate the associated IAM principal.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables — which hold secrets here — are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are returned in cleartext to any caller with basic Lambda read permissions. A customer-managed CMK with a restrictive key policy would be needed to control decryption of these values.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group boundary. Combined with the embedded credentials, compromised or malicious code could exfiltrate data to arbitrary external endpoints.

The assume role policy grants sts:AssumeRole to the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the trust relationship is not scoped to a specific account or function ARN.
